title: Coverage and whole containers
hook: The wall needs 2.3 tins of paint. How many tins do you buy?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

misconception: A fractional material requirement can always be purchased exactly.
objective: Distinguish continuous material need from indivisible container purchases.

claims.text: A fictional coverage label states 8m² per litre. Containers hold 1L; coverage is assumed exact. Scaled model; hypothetical coverage; no application guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by this lesson's declared expressions; each card prints its working in plain words. At Area=18.4m², A=3L and B=2.3L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["ceil",["/","x",8]]; B=["/","x",8]; x denotes Area. At x=10, A=2, B=1.25. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified by demo-builder 2026-10-15 (v2, company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md): v2 stage: plain-words readouts (TP-7a), no 'Full scale' label (TP-7b), money to 2 decimals (TP-7c); A=["ceil", ["/", "x", 8]], B=["/", "x", 8], variable {"label": "Area", "start": 18.4, "min": 4, "max": 30, "unit": "m\u00b2", "step": 0.4}. At Area 18.4m² and 8m² per 1L tin, exact need 18.4/8 = 2.3L; rounded up to whole tins = 3. Slider steps of 0.4m² cross 16m² (2 tins) to 16.4m² (3 tins). | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Own node run of resource-model.ts on the v2 spec: at Area 18.4 m² A = ceil(18.4/8) = 3 and B = 2.3, shown as '3L' / '2.3L'; card A reads '18.4 ÷ 8 = 2.3, rounded up to 3 whole tins', card B '18.4 ÷ 8' (no ceil on screen). 18.4 is a slider stop (4 + 36 × 0.4). Allocation picture: fill = value / resourceGraphicScale (fixed, max over the range). Note for demo-builder: at 4 to 8 m² card A reads 'rounded up to 1 whole tins' (plural). Record: company/reviews/lh-coverage-whole-cans/2026-10-15-fact-check.md, Pass 51.

claims.text: Area divided by coverage gives modeled exact volume. The whole-container order rounds that result up. This ignores surface losses and product variation, so it teaches order arithmetic rather than actual application instructions.

claims.text: A fictional label states 8m² per litre; containers hold 1L and cannot be split. How many containers for 17m²? Correct: 3. 17 ÷ 8 = 2.125L exactly, and whole containers round that up to 3.
